answers.question: what can i fork?
answers.answer:
You can fork "Fork the First Artist," a project built at ETHGlobal Mumbai. It allows any garden artist to hold a name they own under osoartist.eth, have an AI steward on 0G, and use a tip jar. You can run your own artist garden with ENS names and a 0G steward per artist.

The code is open source (GPL-3.0):
https://github.com/Open-Source-Orchestra/fork-the-first-artist

You can also fork the Open Source Orchestra storytelling site:
https://github.com/Open-Source-Orchestra/oso-storytelling

For more, visit the org at https://github.com/Open-Source-Orchestra or Shaka’s 116 public repos at https://github.com/shakaleikaumaka.

Open Source Orchestra

answers.question: Who is Shaka?

Shaka Lei Kaumaka (Shaka 🤙) is a musician playing guitar, ukulele, and voice. He is the founder and human steward of the Open Source Orchestra, a circle of musicians who play open rooms at Ethereum gatherings with no gatekeepers.

He recently played every day of the Devcon 8 Music Sanctuary in Mumbai (Nov 3–6, 2026) and gave a talk titled "In the future music and culture is free" on Nov 6.

Learn more at:

answers.question: What is the Open Source Orchestra DAO?
answers.answer:
The Open Source Orchestra DAO is an open ledger for the circle’s community grants. It lists every application, answer, and award publicly. As of 9 November 2026, it is a community ledger, not yet an on-chain DAO, with a charter being drafted. Grants are received at osoartist.eth and held by Shaka Lei Kaumaka.

Every contribution is equal, and funding asks are shared equally by default unless the circle decides otherwise. You can view the honest status and applications here: https://opensourceorchestra.org/dao/
answers.note: "Funding asks are shared" is garbled: the money that comes in is shared equally by default. Fixed wording.

answers.question: What does every contribution equal mean?
answers.answer:
“Every contribution is equal” means that code, music, art, translation, sound engineering, and stewarding all count the same. Each participant has one voice. Funding asks are made for the whole circle and shared equally by default, though the circle can decide otherwise openly on the ledger. This principle applies to the Open Source Orchestra DAO and its community.

Learn more: https://opensourceorchestra.org/dao/
Join: https://opensourceorchestra.org/join/

answers.question: What's the ukulele's road home?
answers.answer:
The ukulele’s road home traces its journey from Portugal to Hawaiʻi in 1879, then around the world with Shaka. In 2026, it traveled from Japan to China, India (Devcon 8), and Thailand (Chiang Mai), before heading to Portugal for Devcon 9 in 2027. Shaka lets strangers play it, keeping the instrument alive in community hands.

Learn more: https://opensourceorchestra.org/mandala-room/ · https://shakaleikaumaka.com/songbook/
answers.note: Half wrong: it made it sound as if Shaka's own ukulele sailed to Hawaiʻi in 1879. That was the machete of Madeira, the ukulele's ancestor. Fixed: the facts now tell the two parts separately.

Your money is safe because there is no custody. No one holds your funds, there is no escrow, and the Open Source Orchestra takes no cut. I will never ask for, accept, or repeat a seed phrase, private key, or password. I also never move money or share private information. Please do not send your seed phrase to me or anyone else; doing so compromises your security.

For questions about the Open Source Orchestra or Shaka, you can reach out at aloha@myagentohana.com or visit https://opensourceorchestra.org/ .

answers.question: What did you build at ETHGlobal Mumbai?
answers.answer:
I did not build anything at ETHGlobal Mumbai; I am the AI steward for Shaka. Shaka Lei Kaumaka co-built "Fork the First Artist" there with the development team. This project lets every garden artist hold a name they own under osoartist.eth, have an AI steward on 0G that answers only from public facts, and use a tip jar paying 96.31% to the artist.

Live: https://artist.opensourceorchestra.org/
Showcase: https://ethglobal.com/showcase/forkthefirstartist-mk84p

answers.question: Which chains can I tip on?
answers.answer:
You can tip on many Ethereum chains. The available options include Ethereum, Base, OP Mainnet, Arbitrum One, World Chain, Unichain, Ink, Celo, Linea, ZKsync Era, Polygon PoS, BNB Smart Chain, Scroll, Soneium, Zora, and Mode, along with their respective testnets.

Please note that as of today, the multichain tip feature is currently active on testnets only (practice money). Mainnet support will switch on after final safety checks. You can check the public configuration for the current status here: https://artist.opensourceorchestra.org/tip-config.json

For more details on the tipping system, visit: https://artist.opensourceorchestra.org/tip

answers.question: How do I tip the whole orchestra?
answers.answer: To tip the whole Open Source Orchestra, go to https://artist.opensourceorchestra.org/tip. In the tip picker, choose "tip the whole orchestra" (or add &mode=orchestra to the URL). Your wallet sends one amount, which splits across every artist who has set up a wallet. For now, it sends one transfer per wallet, one after another. You can also tip Shaka directly at shaka.osoartist.eth. Mainnet tips are live on 16 chains. More info: https://opensourceorchestra.org/

answers.question: Is my money safe? Who holds custody of my tip?
answers.answer:
Your money is safe because there is no custody. No one holds your money, there is no escrow, and no Open Source Orchestra cut. Your own wallet sends each transfer directly to the artist’s ENS name, and you see it for review first. Never share a seed phrase or private key with anyone, including this steward.

Tip here: https://artist.opensourceorchestra.org/tip

For more details on the DAO and grants: https://opensourceorchestra.org/dao/

answers.question: Is my money safe? Who holds custody of my tip?
answers.answer:
Your money is safe because there is no custody. No one holds your funds, there is no escrow, and the Open Source Orchestra takes no cut. Your own wallet sends each transfer directly to the artist’s ENS name after you review the details.

To protect you, there is a review screen, small per-tip limits (0.01–100 USDC or 0.0001–0.05 ETH), and a public kill switch. Once sent, a transfer is final, so please check the name, chain, and amount before confirming. Never share a seed phrase or private key with anyone.

answers.question: What happened at Devcon 8?
answers.answer:
Shaka Lei Kaumaka played every day of the Devcon 8 Music Sanctuary in Mumbai (Nov 3–6, 2026). About 35 artists gathered in a circle for open jams. On Friday, the Sanctuary hosted the closing ceremony with a brass lamp, confetti, and dancing. Shaka also gave a talk titled "In the future music and culture is free" on Jasmine Stage 4.

For more details, see the schedule archive: https://app.devcon.org/schedule/W8HAES
Or view the photo album: https://opensourceorchestra.org/mandala-room/
